newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat futures end higher on corn rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat futures end higher on corn rally.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher, pulled up by a rally in corn futures, traders said.
"There was spillover input from corn and harvest is winding down," said Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel.
Corn was boosted by forecasts for hotter, drier weather in the U.S. Midwest which could interfere with that crop's key pollination stage of development.
Dry weather in parts of Australia's wheat growing region also buoyed futures but fund buying was pitted against commercial selling, traders said.
Refco Inc bought one million bushels each of September and December, traders said. Continental Grain sold one million bushels of September, sources said.
USDA Monday said as of Sunday the U.S. winter wheat crop was 63 percent harvested, ahead of 61 percent a year ago and ahead of 60 percent average.
Wheat closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with July up three at $3.32. Sep was up 2-1/4 at $3.38-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 22,181 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc bought 100 September $3.30 calls at 16-1/2 to 17 cents and SAK Futures bought 100 September $3.30 puts at seven cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,500 contracts, above the 3,358 traded Monday.
